title: NEET (UG) 2024 · 5 May 2024 · Code T1
instr: NEET (UG) 2024 held on 5 May 2024, Test Booklet Code T1, with the final answer key revised by the National Testing Agency (NTA) on 26 July 2024.

200 questions: Physics 1–50, Chemistry 51–100, Botany 101–150, Zoology 151–200. Each subject has Section A (35 compulsory questions) and Section B (15 questions, of which candidates had to attempt any 10). Each question has four options (1)–(4) with one correct answer.

Marking: +4 for a correct answer, −1 for a wrong answer, 0 if not answered. As in the exam, only the first 10 questions you answer in each Section B are marked, so the maximum is 720 marks (180 questions).

No question was dropped and every question has a single correct answer in the revised key. Q25 (Physics, atoms) was revised by NTA after the Supreme Court order of 23 July 2024: only option (1) is now accepted.
source: Questions: NEET (UG) 2024, Test Booklet Code T1. Answers: NTA final answer key revised on 26 July 2024. Explanations: All in All Exam Practice.

questions.text: A wheel of a bullock cart is rolling on a level road as shown in the figure below. If its linear speed is $v$ in the direction shown, which one of the following options is correct ($P$ and $Q$ are any highest and lowest points on the wheel, respectively)?
options: Both the points $P$ and $Q$ move with equal speed.
questions.sol:
In rolling without slipping, the velocity of any point is the velocity of the centre plus the velocity due to rotation ($\omega R = v$).
At the top $P$: $v + v = 2v$. At the bottom $Q$ (the point in contact): $v - v = 0$.
So $P$ moves faster than $Q$.

questions.text: In the above diagram, a strong bar magnet is moving towards solenoid-2 from solenoid-1. The direction of induced current in solenoid-1 and that in solenoid-2, respectively, are through the directions:
questions.sol:
By Lenz's law each solenoid opposes the change in its flux.
Solenoid-1: the N pole is moving away from end $B$, so end $B$ becomes a S pole (to attract it back). For the winding shown this needs a current from $A$ to $B$.
Solenoid-2: the S pole is approaching end $C$, so end $C$ becomes a S pole (to repel it). For the winding shown this needs a current from $D$ to $C$.
So the currents are $AB$ and $DC$.

questions.text:
Consider the following statements A and B and identify the correct answer :
A. For a solar-cell, the I-V characteristics lies in the IV quadrant of the given graph.
B. In a reverse biased $pn$ junction diode, the current measured in $(\mu A)$, is due to majority charge carriers.
options: Both A and B are correct.
Both A and B are incorrect.
A is correct but B is incorrect.
A is incorrect but B is correct.
questions.sol:
A is correct: a solar cell gives a positive voltage while the current flows in the reverse direction, so its I-V curve is drawn in the fourth quadrant.
B is incorrect: the small reverse current (of the order of $\mu A$) is due to the drift of minority charge carriers.

questions.text: A wire of length ‘$l$’ and resistance $100\ \Omega$ is divided into 10 equal parts. The first 5 parts are connected in series while the next 5 parts are connected in parallel. The two combinations are again connected in series. The resistance of this final combination is:
questions.sol:
Each part has resistance $100/10 = 10\ \Omega$.
Five in series: $5 \times 10 = 50\ \Omega$. Five in parallel: $10/5 = 2\ \Omega$.
In series: $50 + 2 = 52\ \Omega$.
questions.subject: Physics

questions.text: In the following circuit, the equivalent capacitance between terminal $A$ and terminal $B$ is :
questions.sol:
All five capacitors are equal, so the bridge is balanced: the two ends of the middle $2\ \mu F$ capacitor are at the same potential and it holds no charge.
Each arm is two $2\ \mu F$ capacitors in series, i.e. $1\ \mu F$. The two arms in parallel give $1 + 1 = 2\ \mu F$.

questions.text: The output ($Y$) of the given logic gate is similar to the output of an/a :
questions.sol:
The NAND gate with both inputs joined to $A$ gives $\overline{A}$. The NOR gate with both inputs joined to $B$ gives $\overline{B}$.
The final NOR gate gives $Y = \overline{\overline{A} + \overline{B}} = A\cdot B$ (De Morgan's theorem), which is the AND output.

questions.text: The terminal voltage of the battery, whose emf is $10V$ and internal resistance $1\ \Omega$, when connected through an external resistance of $4\ \Omega$ as shown in the figure is :
questions.sol:
Current $I = \dfrac{E}{R + r} = \dfrac{10}{4 + 1} = 2$ A.
Terminal voltage $V = E - Ir = 10 - 2 \times 1 = 8$ V.

questions.text: In a uniform magnetic field of 0.049 T, a magnetic needle performs 20 complete oscillations in 5 seconds as shown. The moment of inertia of the needle is $9.8 \times 10^{-6}\ \text{kg m}^2$. If the magnitude of magnetic moment of the needle is $x \times 10^{-5}\ \text{Am}^2$; then the value of ‘$x$’ is :
questions.sol:
Period $T = 5/20 = 0.25$ s. For a needle oscillating in a field, $T = 2\pi\sqrt{\dfrac{I}{mB}}$, so $m = \dfrac{4\pi^2 I}{T^2 B}$.
$m = \dfrac{4\pi^2 \times 9.8\times10^{-6}}{0.0625 \times 0.049} = 4\pi^2 \times 3.2\times10^{-3} = 1.28\times10^{-2}\pi^2 = 1280\pi^2 \times 10^{-5}\ \text{Am}^2$.
So $x = 1280\pi^2$.

questions.text:
If $c$ is the velocity of light in free space, the correct statements about photon among the following are :
A. The energy of a photon is $E = h\nu$.
B. The velocity of a photon is $c$.
C. The momentum of a photon, $p = \dfrac{h\nu}{c}$.
D. In a photon-electron collision, both total energy and total momentum are conserved.
E. Photon possesses positive charge.
Choose the correct answer from the options given below :
options: A, B, D and E only
A, B, C and D only
questions.sol:
A, B and C are the standard photon relations: $E = h\nu$, speed $c$ in free space, and $p = E/c = h\nu/c$.
D is true: in a photon-electron collision total energy and total momentum are conserved.
E is false: a photon is electrically neutral.
So A, B, C and D only.

questions.text: The maximum elongation of a steel wire of 1 m length if the elastic limit of steel and its Young’s modulus, respectively, are $8 \times 10^{8}\ \text{N m}^{-2}$ and $2 \times 10^{11}\ \text{N m}^{-2}$, is :
questions.sol:
The largest stress the wire can take elastically is the elastic limit, so the maximum strain is $\dfrac{8\times10^{8}}{2\times10^{11}} = 4\times10^{-3}$.
Maximum elongation $= 4\times10^{-3} \times 1\ \text{m} = 4$ mm.

questions.sol: $I = \dfrac{ML^2}{12} \Rightarrow L^2 = \dfrac{12 \times 2400}{400} = 72\ \text{cm}^2$, so $L = \sqrt{72} \approx 8.5$ cm.

questions.text: In a vernier calipers, $(N + 1)$ divisions of vernier scale coincide with $N$ divisions of main scale. If 1 MSD represents 0.1 mm, the vernier constant (in cm) is :
questions.sol:
$(N+1)$ VSD $= N$ MSD, so 1 VSD $= \dfrac{N}{N+1}$ MSD.
Vernier constant $= 1\ \text{MSD} - 1\ \text{VSD} = \dfrac{1}{N+1}$ MSD $= \dfrac{0.1}{N+1}$ mm $= \dfrac{0.01}{N+1}$ cm $= \dfrac{1}{100(N+1)}$ cm.

questions.text:
Match List I with List II.
List I
(Spectral Lines of Hydrogen for transitions from)		List II
(Wavelengths (nm))
A.$n_2 = 3$ to $n_1 = 2$I.410.2
B.$n_2 = 4$ to $n_1 = 2$II.434.1
C.$n_2 = 5$ to $n_1 = 2$III.656.3
D.$n_2 = 6$ to $n_1 = 2$IV.486.1
Choose the correct answer from the options given below :
questions.sol:
These are Balmer lines. The larger the energy gap, the smaller $\lambda$: $3\to2$ gives the longest $\lambda$ (656.3 nm, $H_\alpha$), then $4\to2$ (486.1 nm), $5\to2$ (434.1 nm) and $6\to2$ (410.2 nm).

questions.text: If the monochromatic source in Young’s double slit experiment is replaced by white light, then
options: there will be a central bright white fringe surrounded by a few coloured fringes.
all bright fringes will be of equal width.
there will be a central dark fringe surrounded by a few coloured fringes.
questions.sol: At the centre the path difference is zero for every colour, so all colours reinforce and the central fringe is white. Away from the centre the fringe width ($\propto \lambda$) differs for each colour, so a few coloured fringes are seen before the pattern blurs out.

questions.text: The graph which shows the variation of $\left(\dfrac{1}{\lambda^2}\right)$ and its kinetic energy, $E$ is (where $\lambda$ is de Broglie wavelength of a free particle) :
questions.sol:
$\lambda = \dfrac{h}{p} = \dfrac{h}{\sqrt{2mE}}$, so $\dfrac{1}{\lambda^2} = \dfrac{2m}{h^2}E$.
$\dfrac{1}{\lambda^2}$ is directly proportional to $E$: a straight line through the origin, graph (2).

questions.text: An unpolarised light beam strikes a glass surface at Brewster’s angle. Then
options: both the reflected and refracted light will be completely polarised.
the reflected light will be completely polarised but the refracted light will be partially polarised.
the reflected light will be partially polarised.
the refracted light will be completely polarised.
questions.sol: At Brewster's angle the reflected ray is perpendicular to the refracted ray, and the reflected light is completely plane polarised (vibrations perpendicular to the plane of incidence). The refracted light still contains both components, so it is only partially polarised.

questions.text: A particle moving with uniform speed in a circular path maintains :
questions.sol: In uniform circular motion the speed is constant but the direction of motion changes continuously, so the velocity varies. The centripetal acceleration has constant magnitude $v^2/r$ but always points towards the centre, so its direction (and hence the acceleration vector) also varies.
questions.subject: Physics

questions.text: The quantities which have the same dimensions as those of solid angle are :
questions.sol: Solid angle (area/radius$^2$) is dimensionless. Strain (change in length/length) and plane angle (arc/radius) are also dimensionless. Arc has dimensions of length, angular speed $[T^{-1}]$ and stress $[ML^{-1}T^{-2}]$.
questions.subject: Physics

questions.text: A bob is whirled in a horizontal plane by means of a string with an initial speed of $\omega$ rpm. The tension in the string is $T$. If speed becomes $2\,\omega$ while keeping the same radius, the tension in the string becomes :
questions.sol: The tension provides the centripetal force: $T = m\omega^2 r$. Doubling $\omega$ at the same radius makes the tension $4T$.
questions.subject: Physics

questions.text: If $x = 5\sin\left(\pi t + \dfrac{\pi}{3}\right)m$ represents the motion of a particle executing simple harmonic motion, the amplitude and time period of motion, respectively, are :
questions.sol: Comparing with $x = A\sin(\omega t + \phi)$: $A = 5$ m and $\omega = \pi\ \text{rad s}^{-1}$, so $T = \dfrac{2\pi}{\omega} = 2$ s.
questions.subject: Physics

questions.text: A thermodynamic system is taken through the cycle $abcda$. The work done by the gas along the path $bc$ is :
questions.sol: Along $bc$ the volume stays at $400\ \text{cm}^3$ (a vertical line on the $P$-$V$ diagram), so $\Delta V = 0$ and the work done $W = \int P\,dV = 0$.

questions.text:
Given below are two statements :
$\textbf{Statement I :}$ Atoms are electrically neutral as they contain equal number of positive and negative charges.
$\textbf{Statement II :}$ Atoms of each element are stable and emit their characteristic spectrum.
In the light of the above statements, choose the $\textit{most appropriate}$ answer from the options given below :
options: Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect.
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct.
Both Statement I and Statement II are correct.
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect.
questions.sol:
Statement I is correct: an atom has as many electrons as protons, so it is electrically neutral.
Statement II is not correct as a general statement: not every atom is stable (the nuclei of radioactive elements decay), and an atom emits its characteristic spectrum only when it is excited, not on its own.
So Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect.
questions.subject: Physics
questions.note: NTA's final key of June 2024 accepted two options for this question. After the Supreme Court's order of 23 July 2024, the key revised on 26 July 2024 accepts only option (1).

questions.text: In an ideal transformer, the turns ratio is $\dfrac{N_p}{N_s} = \dfrac{1}{2}$. The ratio $V_s : V_p$ is equal to (the symbols carry their usual meaning) :
questions.sol: For an ideal transformer $\dfrac{V_s}{V_p} = \dfrac{N_s}{N_p} = \dfrac{2}{1}$, so $V_s : V_p = 2 : 1$.
questions.subject: Physics

questions.text: Two bodies A and B of same mass undergo completely inelastic one dimensional collision. The body A moves with velocity $v_1$ while body B is at rest before collision. The velocity of the system after collision is $v_2$. The ratio $v_1 : v_2$ is :
questions.sol: In a completely inelastic collision the bodies move together. Conservation of momentum: $mv_1 = (m + m)v_2$, so $v_1 : v_2 = 2 : 1$.

questions.text:
${}^{290}_{82}X \xrightarrow{\ \alpha\ } Y \xrightarrow{\ e^+\ } Z \xrightarrow{\ \beta^-\ } P \xrightarrow{\ e^-\ } Q$
In the nuclear emission stated above, the mass number and atomic number of the product $Q$ respectively, are :
questions.sol:
Each step is an emission. $\alpha$ emission: $A$ falls by 4 and $Z$ by 2, giving $(286, 80)$. $e^+$ emission: $Z$ falls by 1, giving $(286, 79)$. $\beta^-$ emission: $Z$ rises by 1, giving $(286, 80)$. $e^-$ (another electron emitted): $Z$ rises by 1, giving $(286, 81)$.
So $Q$ has mass number 286 and atomic number 81.
questions.subject: Physics

questions.text:
Given below are two statements: one is labelled as $\textbf{Assertion A}$ and the other is labelled as $\textbf{Reason R.}$
$\textbf{Assertion A}$ : The potential $(V)$ at any axial point, at 2 m distance($r$) from the centre of the dipole of dipole moment vector $\vec{P}$ of magnitude, $4 \times 10^{-6}$ C m, is $\pm 9\times10^{3}\ V$.
(Take $\dfrac{1}{4\pi\epsilon_0} = 9\times10^{9}$ SI units)
$\textbf{Reason R}$ : $V = \pm\dfrac{2P}{4\pi\epsilon_0 r^2}$, where $r$ is the distance of any axial point, situated at 2 m from the centre of the dipole.
In the light of the above statements, choose the $\textit{correct}$ answer from the options given below:
options: A is true but R is false.
A is false but R is true.
Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true and R is NOT the correct explanation of A.
questions.sol:
On the axis of a short dipole $V = \pm\dfrac{P}{4\pi\epsilon_0 r^2} = \pm\dfrac{9\times10^{9} \times 4\times10^{-6}}{2^2} = \pm 9\times10^{3}$ V, so A is true.
R has an extra factor of 2 (that factor belongs to the axial electric field, not the potential), so R is false.
questions.subject: Physics

questions.text:
A thin spherical shell is charged by some source. The potential difference between the two points $C$ and $P$ (in V) shown in the figure is:
(Take $\dfrac{1}{4\pi\epsilon_0} = 9\times10^{9}$ SI units)
questions.sol:
Inside a charged conducting (thin) spherical shell the electric field is zero, so the potential everywhere inside equals the potential on the shell, $\dfrac{q}{4\pi\epsilon_0 R}$.
$C$ (the centre) and $P$ (on the shell) are therefore at the same potential: the potential difference is zero.
questions.subject: Physics

questions.text: A thin flat circular disc of radius 4.5 cm is placed gently over the surface of water. If surface tension of water is $0.07\ \text{Nm}^{-1}$, then the excess force required to take it away from the surface is :
questions.sol:
Surface tension acts along the rim of the disc, whose length is the circumference $2\pi r$.
$F = S \times 2\pi r = 0.07 \times 2 \times \dfrac{22}{7} \times 0.045 = 1.98\times10^{-2}$ N $= 19.8$ mN.
questions.subject: Physics

questions.text: A light ray enters through a right angled prism at point $P$ with the angle of incidence $30^\circ$ as shown in figure. It travels through the prism parallel to its base $BC$ and emerges along the face $AC$. The refractive index of the prism is:
questions.sol:
The prism angle at $A$ is $90^\circ$, so the two refraction angles inside satisfy $r_1 + r_2 = 90^\circ$.
The ray emerges along face $AC$ (grazing emergence), so $r_2$ is the critical angle: $\sin r_2 = \dfrac{1}{\mu}$, hence $\sin r_1 = \cos r_2$.
At $P$: $\sin 30^\circ = \mu \sin r_1 = \mu\cos r_2 \Rightarrow \cos r_2 = \dfrac{1}{2\mu}$.
$\sin^2 r_2 + \cos^2 r_2 = 1 \Rightarrow \dfrac{1}{\mu^2} + \dfrac{1}{4\mu^2} = 1 \Rightarrow \mu^2 = \dfrac{5}{4}$, so $\mu = \dfrac{\sqrt{5}}{2}$.
questions.subject: Physics

questions.text: At any instant of time $t$, the displacement of any particle is given by $2t - 1$ (SI unit) under the influence of force of $5N$. The value of instantaneous power is (in SI unit):
questions.sol:
Velocity $v = \dfrac{d}{dt}(2t - 1) = 2\ \text{m s}^{-1}$.
Power $P = Fv = 5 \times 2 = 10$ W.
questions.subject: Physics

questions.text: A tightly wound 100 turns coil of radius 10 cm carries a current of 7 A. The magnitude of the magnetic field at the centre of the coil is (Take permeability of free space as $4\pi\times10^{-7}$ SI units):
questions.sol: $B = \dfrac{\mu_0 N I}{2R} = \dfrac{4\pi\times10^{-7} \times 100 \times 7}{2 \times 0.1} = 4.4\times10^{-3}$ T $= 4.4$ mT.
questions.subject: Physics

questions.text: A horizontal force 10 $N$ is applied to a block $A$ as shown in figure. The mass of blocks $A$ and $B$ are 2 kg and 3 kg, respectively. The blocks slide over a frictionless surface. The force exerted by block $A$ on block $B$ is :
questions.sol:
Both blocks move together with acceleration $a = \dfrac{F}{m_A + m_B} = \dfrac{10}{5} = 2\ \text{m s}^{-2}$.
The only horizontal force on $B$ is the push from $A$: $F_{AB} = m_B a = 3 \times 2 = 6$ N.
questions.subject: Physics

questions.text: A small telescope has an objective of focal length 140 cm and an eye piece of focal length 5.0 cm. The magnifying power of telescope for viewing a distant object is:
questions.sol: For normal adjustment, $m = \dfrac{f_o}{f_e} = \dfrac{140}{5} = 28$.
questions.subject: Physics

questions.text: Two heaters A and B have power rating of 1 kW and 2 kW, respectively. Those two are first connected in series and then in parallel to a fixed power source. The ratio of power outputs for these two cases is:
questions.sol:
For the same supply voltage, $R = V^2/P$, so $R_A = 2R_B$.
Series: $\dfrac{1}{P_s} = \dfrac{1}{P_A} + \dfrac{1}{P_B} = 1 + \dfrac{1}{2}$, so $P_s = \dfrac{2}{3}$ kW.
Parallel: $P_p = P_A + P_B = 3$ kW.
$P_s : P_p = \dfrac{2}{3} : 3 = 2 : 9$.
questions.subject: Physics

questions.text: If the mass of the bob in a simple pendulum is increased to thrice its original mass and its length is made half its original length, then the new time period of oscillation is $\dfrac{x}{2}$ times its original time period. Then the value of $x$ is:
questions.sol:
$T = 2\pi\sqrt{l/g}$ does not depend on the mass of the bob.
Halving the length gives $T' = \dfrac{T}{\sqrt{2}} = \dfrac{\sqrt{2}}{2}T$, so $x = \sqrt{2}$.
questions.subject: Physics

questions.text: A parallel plate capacitor is charged by connecting it to a battery through a resistor. If I is the current in the circuit, then in the gap between the plates :
options: displacement current of magnitude equal to I flows in a direction opposite to that of I.
displacement current of magnitude greater than I flows but can be in any direction.
displacement current of magnitude equal to I flows in the same direction as I.
questions.sol: While the capacitor charges, the changing electric field between the plates gives a displacement current $I_d = \epsilon_0 \dfrac{d\Phi_E}{dt}$. This equals the conduction current I in the wires and is in the same direction, so the total current is continuous through the circuit.
questions.subject: Physics

questions.text: A metallic bar of Young’s modulus, $0.5 \times 10^{11}\ \text{N m}^{-2}$ and coefficient of linear thermal expansion $10^{-5}\ {}^\circ\text{C}^{-1}$, length 1 m and area of cross-section $10^{-3}\ \text{m}^2$ is heated from $0^\circ$C to $100^\circ$C without expansion or bending. The compressive force developed in it is:
questions.sol:
The bar is prevented from expanding, so the thermal strain $\alpha\Delta T$ is cancelled by a compressive stress $Y\alpha\Delta T$.
$F = YA\alpha\Delta T = 0.5\times10^{11} \times 10^{-3} \times 10^{-5} \times 100 = 5\times10^{4}$ N $= 50\times10^{3}$ N.
questions.subject: Physics

questions.text:
The velocity ($v$) – time ($t$) plot of the motion of a body is shown below :
The acceleration ($a$) – time ($t$) graph that best suits this motion is :
questions.sol:
Acceleration is the slope of the $v$-$t$ graph.
At first $v = 0$ (slope zero, $a = 0$); then $v$ rises at a steady rate (constant positive $a$); then $v$ is constant ($a = 0$); then $v$ falls at a steady rate (constant negative $a$); finally $v = 0$ again ($a = 0$).
Graph (1) shows exactly this.
questions.subject: Physics

questions.text:
The following graph represents the T-V curves of an ideal gas (where T is the temperature and $V$ the volume) at three pressures $P_1$, $P_2$ and $P_3$ compared with those of Charles’s law represented as dotted lines.
Then the correct relation is:
questions.sol:
For an ideal gas $T = \dfrac{P}{nR}V$, so at a fixed volume the curve at higher pressure is at a higher temperature (the slope of the $T$-$V$ line is proportional to $P$).
Drawing a vertical line at any volume, the $P_1$ curve is highest and the $P_3$ curve lowest, so $P_1 > P_2 > P_3$.
questions.subject: Physics

questions.text: A $10\ \mu F$ capacitor is connected to a 210 V, 50 Hz source as shown in figure. The peak current in the circuit is nearly $(\pi = 3.14)$ :
questions.sol:
$X_C = \dfrac{1}{2\pi fC} = \dfrac{1}{2 \times 3.14 \times 50 \times 10\times10^{-6}} = \dfrac{1000}{3.14}\ \Omega$.
$I_{rms} = \dfrac{V_{rms}}{X_C} = \dfrac{210 \times 3.14}{1000} = 0.659$ A, and the peak current $I_0 = \sqrt{2}\,I_{rms} \approx 0.93$ A.
questions.subject: Physics

questions.text: Choose the correct circuit which can achieve the bridge balance.
questions.sol:
The two upper arms are equal (10 $\Omega$ each), so the bridge balances only if the two lower arms are equal: the arm with the 5 $\Omega$ resistor must have a total of 15 $\Omega$ ($\dfrac{10}{10} = \dfrac{15}{5 + R_D}$, so $R_D = 10\ \Omega$).
This needs the diode $D$ to conduct, in series with the 5 $\Omega$ resistor, with a resistance of 10 $\Omega$. In circuit (3) the diode is in series with the 5 $\Omega$ resistor and is forward biased by the cell, so this circuit can be balanced.
questions.subject: Physics
questions.note: The official answer assumes the forward-biased diode has a resistance of 10 $\Omega$; the question gives no value for it.

questions.text: The property which is not of an electromagnetic wave travelling in free space is that :
options: they travel with a speed equal to $\dfrac{1}{\sqrt{\mu_0 \epsilon_0}}$.
they originate from charges moving with uniform speed.
the energy density in electric field is equal to energy density in magnetic field.
questions.sol:
Electromagnetic radiation is produced by accelerated (or oscillating) charges. A charge moving with uniform speed produces only steady electric and magnetic fields, not radiation.
The other three are true: speed $c = 1/\sqrt{\mu_0\epsilon_0}$, the fields are transverse, and the electric and magnetic energy densities are equal.
questions.subject: Physics

questions.text: The minimum energy required to launch a satellite of mass $m$ from the surface of earth of mass $M$ and radius $R$ in a circular orbit at an altitude of $2R$ from the surface of the earth is:
questions.sol:
The orbit radius is $R + 2R = 3R$. Total energy in orbit $= -\dfrac{GMm}{2(3R)} = -\dfrac{GMm}{6R}$. Energy at the surface (ignoring the earth's rotation) $= -\dfrac{GMm}{R}$.
Energy needed $= -\dfrac{GMm}{6R} + \dfrac{GMm}{R} = \dfrac{5GmM}{6R}$.
questions.subject: Physics

questions.text:
If the plates of a parallel plate capacitor connected to a battery are moved close to each other, then
A. the charge stored in it, increases.
B. the energy stored in it, decreases.
C. its capacitance increases.
D. the ratio of charge to its potential remains the same.
E. the product of charge and voltage increases.
Choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below:
questions.sol:
$C = \dfrac{\epsilon_0 A}{d}$ increases as $d$ decreases (C true). The battery keeps $V$ fixed, so $Q = CV$ increases (A true).
Energy $\tfrac{1}{2}CV^2$ increases (B false). $Q/V = C$ changes (D false). $QV = CV^2$ increases (E true).
So A, C and E only.
questions.subject: Physics

questions.text: A force defined by $F = \alpha t^2 + \beta t$ acts on a particle at a given time $t$. The factor which is dimensionless, if $\alpha$ and $\beta$ are constants, is:
questions.sol:
Each term must have the dimensions of force: $[\alpha t^2] = [\beta t] = [F]$.

questions.text:
A sheet is placed on a horizontal surface in front of a strong magnetic pole. A force is needed to :
A. hold the sheet there if it is magnetic.
B. hold the sheet there if it is non-magnetic.
C. move the sheet away from the pole with uniform velocity if it is conducting.
D. move the sheet away from the pole with uniform velocity if it is both, non-conducting and non-polar.
Choose the correct statement(s) from the options given below:
questions.sol:
A: a magnetic sheet is attracted by the pole, so a force is needed to hold it (true).
B: a non-magnetic sheet feels no magnetic force at rest, so no force is needed (false).
C: moving a conducting sheet through the changing field induces eddy currents that oppose the motion, so a force is needed even at uniform velocity (true).
D: a non-conducting, non-polar sheet does not interact with the field (false).
So A and C only.

questions.text: An iron bar of length L has magnetic moment M. It is bent at the middle of its length such that the two arms make an angle $60^\circ$ with each other. The magnetic moment of this new magnet is:

$M = m L$, where $m$ is the pole strength. After bending, the two arms of length $L/2$ with $60^\circ$ between them form two sides of an equilateral triangle, so the distance between the poles is $L/2$.
New moment $= m \times \dfrac{L}{2} = \dfrac{M}{2}$.

$\textbf{Statement I :}$ The boiling point of three isomeric pentanes follows the order
n-pentane > isopentane > neopentane
$\textbf{Statement II :}$ When branching increases, the molecule attains a shape of sphere. This results in smaller surface area for contact, due to which the intermolecular forces between the spherical molecules are weak, thereby lowering the boiling point.
In the light of the above statements, choose the $\textit{most appropriate}$ answer from the options given below:
options: Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect.
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct.
Both Statement I and Statement II are correct.

questions.text: The energy of an electron in the ground state (n = 1) for $\mathrm{He^+}$ ion is –x J, then that for an electron in n = 2 state for $\mathrm{Be^{3+}}$ ion in J is :

Given below are two statements:
$\textbf{Statement I :}$ The boiling point of hydrides of Group 16 elements follow the order
$\mathrm{H_2O > H_2Te > H_2Se > H_2S}$.
$\textbf{Statement II :}$ On the basis of molecular mass, $\mathrm{H_2O}$ is expected to have lower boiling point than the other members of the group but due to the presence of extensive H-bonding in $\mathrm{H_2O}$, it has higher boiling point.
In the light of the above statements, choose the $\textit{correct}$ answer from the options given below:
options: Statement I is true but Statement II is false.
Statement I is false but Statement II is true.
Both Statement I and Statement II are true.
Both Statement I and Statement II are false.
questions.sol:
Down the group the boiling points of $\mathrm{H_2S}$, $\mathrm{H_2Se}$ and $\mathrm{H_2Te}$ rise with molecular mass (stronger van der Waals forces), so $\mathrm{H_2Te > H_2Se > H_2S}$.
$\mathrm{H_2O}$ has the lowest molecular mass but extensive hydrogen bonding gives it by far the highest boiling point. So both statements are true.

The reagents with which glucose does $\textbf{not}$ react to give the corresponding tests/products are
A. Tollen’s reagent
B. Schiff’s reagent
C. HCN
D. $\mathrm{NH_2OH}$
E. $\mathrm{NaHSO_3}$
Choose the correct options from the given below:
questions.sol:
Glucose gives a silver mirror with Tollen's reagent, a cyanohydrin with HCN and an oxime with $\mathrm{NH_2OH}$.
Although it has an aldehyde group, glucose does not give Schiff's test and does not form the hydrogensulphite addition product with $\mathrm{NaHSO_3}$; this is evidence that the aldehyde group is mostly present in the cyclic (hemiacetal) form. So B and E.

Arrange the following elements in increasing order of first ionization enthalpy:
Li, Be, B, C, N
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.sol:
Ionisation enthalpy generally rises across period 2, but B ($2s^2 2p^1$) is lower than Be ($2s^2$): the $2p$ electron of B is less penetrating and is more easily removed than a $2s$ electron.
So Li (520) < B (801) < Be (899) < C (1086) < N (1402 kJ mol$^{-1}$).

questions.text:
For the reaction $\mathrm{2A \rightleftharpoons B + C}$, $\mathrm{K_c = 4\times10^{-3}}$. At a given time, the composition of reaction mixture is : $\mathrm{[A] = [B] = [C] = 2\times10^{-3}\ M}$.
Then, which of the following is correct?
options: Reaction has a tendency to go in backward direction.
Reaction has gone to completion in forward direction.
Reaction has a tendency to go in forward direction.
questions.sol:
Reaction quotient $Q_c = \dfrac{[B][C]}{[A]^2} = \dfrac{(2\times10^{-3})(2\times10^{-3})}{(2\times10^{-3})^2} = 1$.
$Q_c = 1 > K_c = 4\times10^{-3}$, so there are too many products and the reaction tends to go in the backward direction.

By Henry's law $p = K_H x$, so at a given pressure the solubility (mole fraction) is inversely proportional to $K_H$.

questions.text:
Given below are two statements :
$\textbf{Statement I :}$ Both $\mathrm{\left[Co(NH_3)_6\right]^{3+}}$ and $\mathrm{\left[CoF_6\right]^{3-}}$ complexes are octahedral but differ in their magnetic behaviour.
$\textbf{Statement II :}$ $\mathrm{\left[Co(NH_3)_6\right]^{3+}}$ is diamagnetic whereas $\mathrm{\left[CoF_6\right]^{3-}}$ is paramagnetic.
In the light of the above statements, choose the $\textit{correct}$ answer from the options given below:
options: Statement I is true but Statement II is false.
Statement I is false but Statement II is true.
Both Statement I and Statement II are true.
Both Statement I and Statement II are false.
questions.sol:
Both complexes contain $\mathrm{Co^{3+}}$ ($3d^6$) with six ligands, so both are octahedral.
$\mathrm{NH_3}$ is a strong field ligand: the six $d$ electrons pair up in the $t_{2g}$ set ($d^2sp^3$, inner orbital), so $\mathrm{[Co(NH_3)_6]^{3+}}$ is diamagnetic.
$\mathrm{F^-}$ is a weak field ligand: $t_{2g}^4e_g^2$ with four unpaired electrons ($sp^3d^2$, outer orbital), so $\mathrm{[CoF_6]^{3-}}$ is paramagnetic. Both statements are true.

B. Temperature of a crystalline solid lowered from 130 K to 0 K.

questions.text:
Consider the following reaction in a sealed vessel at equilibrium with concentrations of
$\mathrm{N_2 = 3.0 \times 10^{-3}\ M}$, $\mathrm{O_2 = 4.2 \times 10^{-3}\ M}$ and $\mathrm{NO = 2.8 \times 10^{-3}\ M}$.
$\mathrm{2NO_{(g)} \rightleftharpoons N_{2(g)} + O_{2(g)}}$
If 0.1 mol $\mathrm{L^{-1}}$ of $\mathrm{NO_{(g)}}$ is taken in a closed vessel, what will be degree of dissociation $(\alpha)$ of $\mathrm{NO_{(g)}}$ at equilibrium?
questions.sol:
$K_c = \dfrac{[N_2][O_2]}{[NO]^2} = \dfrac{3.0\times10^{-3} \times 4.2\times10^{-3}}{(2.8\times10^{-3})^2} = \dfrac{12.6}{7.84} = 1.607$.
Starting with 0.1 M NO: at equilibrium $[NO] = 0.1(1 - \alpha)$ and $[N_2] = [O_2] = 0.05\alpha$.
$\dfrac{0.05\alpha}{0.1(1 - \alpha)} = \sqrt{1.607} = 1.268 \Rightarrow \alpha = 2.536(1 - \alpha) \Rightarrow \alpha = \dfrac{2.536}{3.536} = 0.717$.

questions.text:
The plot of osmotic pressure ($\Pi$) vs concentration (mol $\mathrm{L^{-1}}$) for a solution gives a straight line with slope 25.73 L bar $\mathrm{mol^{-1}}$. The temperature at which the osmotic pressure measurement is done is:
(Use R = 0.083 L bar $\mathrm{mol^{-1}\ K^{-1}}$)
questions.sol:
$\Pi = CRT$, so the slope of $\Pi$ against $C$ is $RT$.
$T = \dfrac{25.73}{0.083} = 310$ K $= 310 - 273 = 37$°C.
questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.text: Identify the major product C formed in the following reaction sequence :
questions.sol:
$\mathrm{CH_3CH_2CH_2I + NaCN \rightarrow CH_3CH_2CH_2CN}$ (A, butanenitrile).
Partial hydrolysis gives the amide $\mathrm{CH_3CH_2CH_2CONH_2}$ (B, butanamide).
$\mathrm{Br_2}$/NaOH (Hoffmann bromamide degradation) gives an amine with one carbon fewer: $\mathrm{CH_3CH_2CH_2NH_2}$ (C, propylamine).

questions.text:
A compound X contains 32% of A, 20% of B and remaining percentage of C. Then, the empirical formula of X is :
(Given atomic masses of A = 64; B = 40; C = 32 u)
questions.sol:
C is $100 - 32 - 20 = 48\%$.
Moles in 100 g: A $= 32/64 = 0.5$; B $= 20/40 = 0.5$; C $= 48/32 = 1.5$.
Ratio A : B : C $= 1 : 1 : 3$, so the empirical formula is $\mathrm{ABC_3}$.

questions.text:
The rate of a reaction quadruples when temperature changes from 27°C to 57°C. Calculate the energy of activation.
Given R = 8.314 J $\mathrm{K^{-1}\ mol^{-1}}$, log 4 = 0.6021
questions.sol:
$\log\dfrac{k_2}{k_1} = \dfrac{E_a}{2.303R}\left(\dfrac{T_2 - T_1}{T_1T_2}\right)$ with $T_1 = 300$ K, $T_2 = 330$ K.
$0.6021 = \dfrac{E_a}{2.303 \times 8.314} \times \dfrac{30}{300 \times 330}$
$E_a = \dfrac{0.6021 \times 2.303 \times 8.314 \times 3300}{1} \approx 38\,044$ J mol$^{-1}$ $= 38.04$ kJ/mol.

questions.text: Identify the $\textbf{correct}$ answer.
options: Dipole moment of $\mathrm{NF_3}$ is greater than that of $\mathrm{NH_3}$.
Three canonical forms can be drawn for $\mathrm{CO_3^{2-}}$ ion.
Three resonance structures can be drawn for ozone.
questions.sol:
The carbonate ion has three equivalent canonical forms (the C=O double bond can be on any of the three oxygens), so (2) is correct.
(1) is wrong: in $\mathrm{NH_3}$ the lone pair moment adds to the N–H bond moments, but in $\mathrm{NF_3}$ it opposes the N–F bond moments, so $\mathrm{NH_3}$ has the larger dipole moment. (3) is wrong: ozone has two resonance structures. (4) is wrong: trigonal planar $\mathrm{BF_3}$ has zero dipole moment.
questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.text: The pair of lanthanoid ions which are diamagnetic is
questions.sol:
A diamagnetic ion has no unpaired electrons: an empty ($4f^0$) or full ($4f^{14}$) $4f$ subshell.
$\mathrm{Ce^{4+}}$ is $4f^0$ and $\mathrm{Yb^{2+}}$ is $4f^{14}$, so both are diamagnetic. The other ions ($\mathrm{Gd^{3+}}$ $4f^7$, $\mathrm{Eu^{3+}}$ $4f^6$, $\mathrm{Pm^{3+}}$ $4f^4$, $\mathrm{Sm^{3+}}$ $4f^5$, $\mathrm{Ce^{3+}}$ $4f^1$, $\mathrm{Eu^{2+}}$ $4f^7$) have unpaired electrons.
questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.text:
Given below are two statements :
$\textbf{Statement I :}$ $\mathrm{\left[Co(NH_3)_6\right]^{3+}}$ is a homoleptic complex whereas $\mathrm{\left[Co(NH_3)_4Cl_2\right]^{+}}$ is a heteroleptic complex.
$\textbf{Statement II :}$ Complex $\mathrm{\left[Co(NH_3)_6\right]^{3+}}$ has only one kind of ligands but $\mathrm{\left[Co(NH_3)_4Cl_2\right]^{+}}$ has more than one kind of ligands.
In the light of the above statements, choose the $\textit{correct}$ answer from the options given below:
options: Statement I is true but Statement II is false.
Statement I is false but Statement II is true.
Both Statement I and Statement II are true.
Both Statement I and Statement II are false.
questions.sol:
A homoleptic complex has only one kind of ligand and a heteroleptic complex has more than one kind.
$\mathrm{[Co(NH_3)_6]^{3+}}$ has only $\mathrm{NH_3}$ (homoleptic), while $\mathrm{[Co(NH_3)_4Cl_2]^+}$ has $\mathrm{NH_3}$ and $\mathrm{Cl^-}$ (heteroleptic). Both statements are true.
questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.text:
Mass in grams of copper deposited by passing 9.6487 A current through a voltmeter containing copper sulphate solution for 100 seconds is:
(Given : Molar mass of Cu : 63 g $\mathrm{mol^{-1}}$, 1F = 96487 C)
questions.sol:
Charge $Q = It = 9.6487 \times 100 = 964.87$ C $= 0.01$ F.
$\mathrm{Cu^{2+} + 2e^- \rightarrow Cu}$, so 2 F deposit 63 g. Mass $= \dfrac{0.01}{2} \times 63 = 0.315$ g.

questions.text: In the given figure, which component has thin outer walls and highly thickened inner walls?
questions.sol:
The figure shows a stoma in surface view: A is an epidermal cell, B a subsidiary cell, C a guard cell and D the stomatal pore.
Each bean-shaped guard cell has a thin, elastic outer wall and a highly thickened inner wall (the one facing the pore). So the answer is C.

questions.text: List of endangered species was released by-
questions.sol: The IUCN (International Union for Conservation of Nature and Natural Resources) publishes the Red List (Red Data Book), which lists threatened and endangered species.
questions.subject: Botany

questions.text: The type of conservation in which the threatened species are taken out from their natural habitat and placed in special setting where they can be protected and given special care is called;
questions.sol: Taking threatened species out of their natural habitat and protecting them in special settings (zoos, botanical gardens, seed banks) is $\textit{ex situ}$ conservation. That option is not offered; of the choices given, it is a form of biodiversity conservation, so option (4) is the intended answer. It is not $\textit{in situ}$ conservation, which protects species within their natural habitat.
questions.subject: Botany

questions.text:
Which one of the following can be explained on the basis of Mendel's Law of Dominance?
A. Out of one pair of factors one is dominant and the other is recessive.
B. Alleles do not show any expression and both the characters appear as such in $F_2$ generation.
C. Factors occur in pairs in normal diploid plants.
D. The discrete unit controlling a particular character is called factor.
E. The expression of only one of the parental characters is found in a monohybrid cross.
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
options: A, B, C, D and E
A, C, D and E only
questions.sol:
The Law of Dominance states that characters are controlled by discrete units called factors (D), which occur in pairs (C), and that in a dissimilar pair one factor dominates the other (A). This explains why only one parental character is expressed in the $F_1$ of a monohybrid cross (E).
B is wrong: alleles do express, and the recessive character reappears in $F_2$ because of segregation, not dominance. So A, C, D and E only.
questions.subject: Botany

questions.text: The lactose present in the growth medium of bacteria is transported to the cell by the action of:
questions.sol: In the $\textit{lac}$ operon, the $\textit{y}$ gene codes for permease, which increases the permeability of the cell to lactose ($\beta$-galactosides). $\beta$-galactosidase hydrolyses lactose and transacetylase is the third enzyme.
questions.subject: Botany

questions.sol: $\textit{Clostridium butylicum}$ produces butyric acid (A-III); $\textit{Saccharomyces cerevisiae}$ (brewer's yeast) produces ethanol (B-I); $\textit{Trichoderma polysporum}$ produces cyclosporin A, an immunosuppressant (C-IV); $\textit{Streptococcus}$ gives streptokinase, a clot buster (D-II).

The equation of Verhulst-Pearl logistic growth is $\dfrac{dN}{dt} = rN\left[\dfrac{K-N}{K}\right]$.
From this equation, $K$ indicates:

questions.sol: A transcription unit has a promoter (towards the upstream end of the structural gene), the structural gene, and a terminator (towards the downstream end).
questions.subject: Botany

questions.sol: Living differentiated cells that have lost the ability to divide can regain it; this is dedifferentiation. Formation of interfascicular cambium (and cork cambium) from fully differentiated parenchyma cells is the standard example.

C.$\textit{Puccinia}$III.Bread mould

questions.sol: $\textit{Rhizopus}$ is the bread mould (A-III), $\textit{Ustilago}$ the smut fungus (B-II), $\textit{Puccinia}$ the rust fungus (C-IV) and $\textit{Agaricus}$ the mushroom (D-I).

questions.text:
What is the fate of a piece of DNA carrying only gene of interest which is transferred into an alien organism?
A. The piece of DNA would be able to multiply itself independently in the progeny cells of the organism.
B. It may get integrated into the genome of the recipient.
C. It may multiply and be inherited along with the host DNA.
D. The alien piece of DNA is not an integral part of chromosome.
E. It shows ability to replicate.
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.sol:
A piece of DNA carrying only the gene of interest has no origin of replication, so it cannot multiply on its own in the alien organism (A and E are wrong, and D describes a plasmid-like state it cannot maintain).
It may, however, get integrated into the recipient's genome (B) and then multiply and be inherited along with the host DNA (C). So B and C only.
questions.subject: Botany

questions.text:
Match List I with List II
List IList II
A.NucleolusI.Site of formation of glycolipid
B.CentrioleII.Organization like the cartwheel
C.LeucoplastsIII.Site for active ribosomal RNA synthesis
D.Golgi apparatusIV.For storing nutrients
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.sol: The nucleolus is the site of active ribosomal RNA synthesis (A-III). A centriole has a cartwheel-like organisation of nine peripheral triplet fibrils (B-II). Leucoplasts are colourless plastids that store nutrients such as starch, oils and proteins (C-IV). The Golgi apparatus is the site of formation of glycoproteins and glycolipids (D-I).
questions.subject: Botany

questions.text: Identify the type of flowers based on the position of calyx, corolla and androecium with respect to the ovary from the given figures (a) and (b)
questions.sol: In both flowers the thalamus forms a cup and the sepals, petals and stamens arise from its rim, at about the level of the ovary; the ovary is not fused with the cup (it is half inferior). This is the perigynous condition, as in plum and rose (NCERT figures of perigynous flowers). So both (a) and (b) are perigynous.

questions.sol: Metaphase begins with the attachment of spindle fibres to the kinetochores of the chromosomes, which then line up at the metaphase plate.

questions.text:
These are regarded as major causes of biodiversity loss:
A. Over exploitation
B. Co-extinction
C. Mutation
D. Habitat loss and fragmentation
E. Migration
Choose the correct option:
options: A, B, C and D only
questions.sol: The four major causes of biodiversity loss (the 'Evil Quartet') are habitat loss and fragmentation, over-exploitation, alien species invasions and co-extinctions. Mutation and migration are not among them. So A, B and D only.
questions.subject: Botany

questions.text: Lecithin, a small molecular weight organic compound found in living tissues, is an example of:
questions.sol: Lecithin is a phospholipid: glycerol esterified with fatty acids and a phosphate group linked to choline.

questions.text:
Identify the set of correct statements:
A. The flowers of $\textit{Vallisneria}$ are colourful and produce nectar.
B. The flowers of waterlily are not pollinated by water.
C. In most of water-pollinated species, the pollen grains are protected from wetting.
D. Pollen grains of some hydrophytes are long and ribbon like.
E. In some hydrophytes, the pollen grains are carried passively inside water.
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
options: A, C, D and E only
B, C, D and E only
A, B, C and D only
questions.sol:
A is wrong: water-pollinated flowers such as $\textit{Vallisneria}$ are not colourful and do not produce nectar.
B is right: waterlily and water hyacinth emerge above water and are pollinated by insects or wind.
C is right: pollen of most water-pollinated species has a mucilaginous covering that protects it from wetting.
D is right: in seagrasses such as $\textit{Zostera}$ the pollen is long and ribbon-like.
E is right: the pollen is carried passively inside the water. So B, C, D and E only.
questions.subject: Botany

questions.text: The cofactor of the enzyme carboxypeptidase is:
questions.sol: Zinc is the metal ion cofactor of the proteolytic enzyme carboxypeptidase.
questions.subject: Botany

questions.text: Inhibition of Succinic dehydrogenase enzyme by malonate is a classical example of:
questions.sol: Malonate closely resembles the substrate succinate and competes with it for the active site of succinic dehydrogenase. This is competitive inhibition.
questions.subject: Botany

questions.text: Which of the following is an example of actinomorphic flower?
questions.sol: An actinomorphic flower can be divided into two equal halves by any radial plane through the centre, as in mustard, $\textit{Datura}$ and chilli. $\textit{Pisum}$, $\textit{Sesbania}$ and $\textit{Cassia}$ have zygomorphic flowers.
questions.subject: Botany

questions.text:
Given below are two statements:
$\textbf{Statement I :}$ Chromosomes become gradually visible under light microscope during leptotene stage.
$\textbf{Statement II :}$ The begining of diplotene stage is recognized by dissolution of synaptonemal complex.
In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below:
options: Statement I is true but Statement II is false
Statement I is false but Statement II is true
Both Statement I and Statement II are true
Both Statement I and Statement II are false
questions.sol:
During leptotene the chromosomes become gradually visible under the light microscope as they condense, so Statement I is true.
Diplotene begins with the dissolution of the synaptonemal complex, after which the homologues tend to separate except at the chiasmata, so Statement II is also true.
questions.subject: Botany

questions.text: A pink flowered Snapdragon plant was crossed with a red flowered Snapdragon plant. What type of phenotype/s is/are expected in the progeny?
options: Red, Pink as well as white flowered plants
Red flowered as well as pink flowered plants
questions.sol:
Flower colour in snapdragon shows incomplete dominance: RR is red, Rr pink and rr white.
Pink (Rr) $\times$ red (RR) gives RR and Rr in a 1 : 1 ratio, i.e. red and pink flowered plants only.
questions.subject: Botany

questions.text:
Given below are two statements:
$\textbf{Statement I :}$ Parenchyma is living but collenchyma is dead tissue.
$\textbf{Statement II :}$ Gymnosperms lack xylem vessels but presence of xylem vessels is the characteristic of angiosperms.
In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below:
options: Statement I is true but Statement II is false
Statement I is false but Statement II is true
Both Statement I and Statement II are true
Both Statement I and Statement II are false
questions.sol:
Both parenchyma and collenchyma are living tissues (sclerenchyma is the dead simple tissue), so Statement I is false.
Gymnosperms lack vessels in their xylem, and the presence of vessels is a characteristic feature of angiosperms, so Statement II is true.
questions.subject: Botany

questions.text:
Given below are two statements:
$\textbf{Statement I :}$ Bt toxins are insect group specific and coded by a gene $\textit{cry}$ IAc.
$\textbf{Statement II :}$ Bt toxin exists as inactive protoxin in $\textit{B. thuringiensis}$. However, after ingestion by the insect the inactive protoxin gets converted into active form due to acidic pH of the insect gut.
In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below:
options: Statement I is true but Statement II is false
Statement I is false but Statement II is true
Both Statement I and Statement II are true
Both Statement I and Statement II are false
questions.sol:
Bt toxins are specific to insect groups and are coded by $\textit{cry}$ genes; $\textit{cry}$IAc (with $\textit{cry}$IIAb) controls cotton bollworms. So Statement I is true.
The inactive protoxin is converted into the active toxin in the $\textbf{alkaline}$ pH of the insect gut, not an acidic one, so Statement II is false.
questions.subject: Botany

questions.text: Which one of the following is $\underline{\text{not}}$ a criterion for classification of fungi?
questions.sol: Kingdom Fungi is divided into classes on the basis of the morphology of the mycelium, the mode of spore formation and the fruiting bodies. Mode of nutrition is not used, as all fungi are heterotrophic.
questions.subject: Botany

questions.text: The capacity to generate a whole plant from any cell of the plant is called:
questions.sol: The capacity of a plant cell (or explant) to generate a whole plant is called totipotency; it is the basis of plant tissue culture and micropropagation.
questions.subject: Botany

questions.text:
Which of the following are required for the dark reaction of photosynthesis?
A. Light
B. Chlorophyll
C. $\mathrm{CO_2}$
D. ATP
E. NADPH
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.sol: The dark (biosynthetic) reactions of the Calvin cycle do not directly need light or chlorophyll. They fix $\mathrm{CO_2}$ using the ATP and NADPH made in the light reactions. So C, D and E only.
questions.subject: Botany

questions.text:
Tropical regions show greatest level of species richness because
A. Tropical latitudes have remained relatively undisturbed for millions of years, hence more time was available for species diversification.
B. Tropical environments are more seasonal.
C. More solar energy is available in tropics.
D. Constant environments promote niche specialization.
E. Tropical environments are constant and predictable.
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
options: A, C, D and E only
questions.sol:
The reasons given in NCERT for high tropical diversity are: the tropics have stayed relatively undisturbed for millions of years, giving more time for species diversification (A); tropical environments are less seasonal, relatively constant and predictable (E), which promotes niche specialisation (D); and more solar energy is available, giving higher productivity (C).
B is wrong, since tropical environments are less seasonal. So A, C, D and E only.
questions.subject: Botany

questions.text: Identify the part of the seed from the given figure which is destined to form root when the seed germinates.
questions.sol: The figure is a longitudinal section of a monocot (maize-type) seed. The root is formed by the radicle. In the figure the radicle is the part labelled C, enclosed in its sheath, the coleorhiza (D); A is the coleoptile and B the shoot apex (plumule). So the answer is C.
questions.subject: Botany

questions.text: How many molecules of ATP and NADPH are required for every molecule of $\mathrm{CO_2}$ fixed in the Calvin cycle?
options: 3 molecules of ATP and 3 molecules of NADPH
3 molecules of ATP and 2 molecules of NADPH
2 molecules of ATP and 3 molecules of NADPH
2 molecules of ATP and 2 molecules of NADPH
questions.sol: Fixing one $\mathrm{CO_2}$ in the Calvin cycle uses 3 ATP (2 in reduction and 1 in regeneration of RuBP) and 2 NADPH (in reduction). Making one glucose (6 $\mathrm{CO_2}$) needs 18 ATP and 12 NADPH.
questions.subject: Botany

questions.text: In a plant, black seed color (BB/Bb) is dominant over white seed color (bb). In order to find out the genotype of the black seed plant, with which of the following genotype will you cross it?
questions.sol: The genotype of a plant showing the dominant phenotype is found by a test cross with the homozygous recessive (bb). If all the progeny are black the plant is BB; if black and white appear in a 1 : 1 ratio it is Bb.

questions.text: Hind II always cuts DNA molecules at a particular point called recognition sequence and it consists of:
questions.sol: $\textit{Hind}$ II, the first restriction endonuclease isolated, always cuts DNA at a particular point by recognising a specific sequence of six base pairs, its recognition sequence.

questions.text: Bulliform cells are responsible for
options: Providing large spaces for storage of sugars.
Inward curling of leaves in monocots.
Protecting the plant from salt stress.
questions.sol: Bulliform cells are large, empty, colourless cells in the upper epidermis of grass (monocot) leaves. When they are turgid the leaf surface is exposed; when they lose water (under water stress) the leaves curl inwards to reduce water loss.
questions.subject: Botany

can help in cell division in grasses, to produce growth.
promotes abscission of mature leaves only.

options: Wind pollinated plant inflorescence showing flowers with well exposed stamens.

C.Paul EhrlichIII.Global species diversity at about 7 million

Paul Ehrlich proposed the rivet popper hypothesis (C-IV). David Tilman carried out long-term ecosystem experiments using outdoor plots (D-II).

questions.text:
Given below are two statements:
$\textbf{Statement I :}$ In $\mathrm{C_3}$ plants, some $\mathrm{O_2}$ binds to RuBisCO, hence $\mathrm{CO_2}$ fixation is decreased.
$\textbf{Statement II :}$ In $\mathrm{C_4}$ plants, mesophyll cells show very little photorespiration while bundle sheath cells do not show photorespiration.
In the light of the above statements, choose the $\textit{correct}$ answer from the options given below:
options: Statement I is true but Statement II is false
Statement I is false but Statement II is true
Both Statement I and Statement II are true
Both Statement I and Statement II are false
questions.sol:
In $\mathrm{C_3}$ plants some $\mathrm{O_2}$ binds to RuBisCO (photorespiration), so $\mathrm{CO_2}$ fixation decreases: Statement I is true.
In $\mathrm{C_4}$ plants the mesophyll cells lack RuBisCO, so they cannot photorespire, and the bundle sheath cells have a high $\mathrm{CO_2}$ concentration around RuBisCO, which keeps photorespiration minimal. Statement II has this the wrong way round, so it is false.

questions.text: Identify the step in tricarboxylic acid cycle, which does not involve oxidation of substrate.
questions.sol:
Isocitrate to $\alpha$-ketoglutarate (oxidative decarboxylation, NADH formed), succinate to fumarate on the way to malate ($\mathrm{FADH_2}$ formed) and malate to oxaloacetate (NADH formed) are all oxidations.
Succinyl-CoA to succinic acid is not an oxidation: the energy of the thioester bond is used to make GTP (ATP) by substrate-level phosphorylation.

B.GlycolysisII.Mitochondrial matrix

questions.text:

In the members of Phaeophyceae,

questions.text: Which of the following statement is correct regarding the process of replication in $\textit{E.coli}$?
options: The DNA dependent DNA polymerase catalyses polymerization in $5' \rightarrow 3'$ as well as $3' \rightarrow 5'$ direction.
The DNA dependent DNA polymerase catalyses polymerization in $5' \rightarrow 3'$ direction.
The DNA dependent DNA polymerase catalyses polymerization in one direction that is $3' \rightarrow 5'$.
The DNA dependent RNA polymerase catalyses polymerization in one direction, that is $5' \rightarrow 3'$.
questions.sol: Replication uses DNA-dependent DNA polymerase, which can polymerise only in the $5' \rightarrow 3'$ direction. This is why one strand (the leading strand) is made continuously and the other (the lagging strand) discontinuously. RNA polymerase is used in transcription, not replication.

questions.text: Spraying sugarcane crop with which of the following plant growth regulators, increases the length of stem, thus, increasing the yield?
questions.sol: Sugarcane stores sugar (sucrose) in its stem. Spraying the crop with gibberellins increases the length of the stem, raising the yield by as much as 20 tonnes per acre.

questions.text: In an ecosystem if the Net Primary Productivity (NPP) of first trophic level is $100x\ (kcal\ m^{-2})\ yr^{-1}$, what would be the GPP (Gross Primary Productivity) of the third trophic level of the same ecosystem?
questions.sol: The reasoning behind the official answer: the net productivity of the first trophic level ($100x$) is what is available to the second trophic level, i.e. it becomes the gross productivity of the second level. By the 10 per cent law only about one-tenth of that is passed on, so the gross productivity of the third trophic level is $100x \times \dfrac{10}{100} = 10x\ (kcal\ m^{-2})\ yr^{-1}$.
questions.subject: Botany
questions.note: Strictly, gross primary productivity belongs only to producers, so the question is loosely worded; the NTA key gives option (1), 10x, treating the first level's NPP as the second level's gross productivity.

questions.text:
Given below are two statements :
$\textbf{Statement I :}$ Gause’s competitive exclusion principle states that two closely related species competing for different resources cannot exist indefinitely.
$\textbf{Statement II :}$ According to Gause’s principle, during competition, the inferior will be eliminated. This may be true if resources are limiting.
In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below :
options: Statement I is true but Statement II is false.
Statement I is false but Statement II is true.
Both Statement I and Statement II are true.
Both Statement I and Statement II are false.
questions.sol:
Statement I is false: Gause’s principle says that two closely related species competing for the $\textit{same}$ resources cannot coexist indefinitely; species using different resources can coexist.
Statement II is true: the competitively inferior species is eventually eliminated, and this may be true when resources are limiting.
